subject: Proposal: graded commit tiers + pilot credits for Veridian POC
body:
Message 1 --- From: Elena Rossi <elena@veridian.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Subject: Quick: pilot credits & commit thresholds question

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Patrick and I ran it by our infra team and were excited to move forward with a technical POC. A few procurement/finance items came up that I want to confirm before I loop in legal:

- Are you able to provide time-limited credits for a 45- to 90-day POC? Were asking for a partner-grade pilot where we test peak token volumes.
- How do per-token discounts stack with reserved commit tiers? For example: if we commit to $100k/month, is the hosted per-token rate discounted in addition to providing credits, or do credits replace pricing concessions?
- Any minimum commitment ramp (months 1-3) youd recommend for a startup in our position?

Appreciate a quick note on how you normally structure these so I can prepare the internal ask.

Best,
Elena Rossi\Head of Platform, Veridian AI

---

Message 2 --- From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:08:00 -0700
To: Elena Rossi <elena@veridian.ai>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Subject: Re: Quick: pilot credits & commit thresholds question

Hi Elena — great to hear youre ready to run a POC. Short answers up front, then a proposed structure attached.

1) Pilot credits: yes — we can offer time-limited hosted API credits that apply across text generation and embeddings. Typical pilot: $15k-$35k in credits for 45 days; larger pilots get $50k+ credits and up to 90 days.

2) Pricing vs credits: credits are additive to discounted per-token pricing for committed deals. We treat credits as an up-front promotional balance applied to usage; discounts reduce per-token unit price going forward. Example in the attachment.

3) Ramp recommendation: 3-month graded commit ramp is common — tiered commit where month 1 = 30% of committed volume, month 2 = 60%, month 3 = 100%. We can be flexible on duration if you need longer runway for integration.

I attached a short sheet (redwood_commit_credit_sheet_v2.pdf) that shows a few examples and a recommended pilot + commit offer for Veridian. If youre ok, next step would be a mutual action plan (MAP) and a short PO/LOI to lock the credits.

Please ping with a couple windows and I can get legal to prepare the simple pilot terms.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole\Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0142

Attachment: redwood_commit_credit_sheet_v2.pdf (PDF, 28KB)

---

Message 3 --- From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 12:04:00 -0700
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Subject: RE: Quick: pilot credits & commit thresholds question

Marissa / Dev —

Saw Marissa's note to Veridian. A couple internal checks:
- Legal: standard pilot T&Cs, data retention and logging clauses ok for hosted API POC? We may need to require the org to use a dedicated API key and accept our standard DPA.
- Finance: credits of $50k+ should require a short-term PO or minimum committed MRR after pilot. Can we allow a refundable hold or credit-card-backed PO?

Dev, can you confirm if the credits mechanics work with our billing flows (apply credit then bill discounted post-commit) and whether the credits can be split across multiple teams in the same account?

Thanks,
Dylan

---

Message 4 --- From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 13:47:00 -0700
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Subject: RE: Quick: pilot credits & commit thresholds question

All good from infra/billing side. Notes:
- Credits are created as a balance on the account that is consumed before card/billing. They can be time-limited and split across sub-accounts (we support seat-level & project-level allocation).
- Discount stacking: for committed customers we apply the committed per-token discount first to compute invoiceable usage, then available credits are debited from the invoice until exhausted. That matches Marissa's outline.
- We can attach a MAP and simple PO id field so Finance can tie credit draw to an executed PO.

Will revisit if legal flags anything, but engineering-wise were fine.

— Dev Patel
Head of Billing Integrations
Redwood Inference

---

Message 5 --- From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 15:48:00 -0700
To: Elena Rossi <elena@veridian.ai>, Patrick O'Neill <patrick.oneill@veridian.ai>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Subject: Re: Quick: pilot credits & commit thresholds question

Elena / Patrick — thanks for the quick turn. Based on your expected peak token estimate and what you said about production timing, heres a recommended, binding-optional proposal: 

Offer (Veridian POC -> Launch):
- Pilot phase (45 days): $30,000 hosted API credits applied to your account. Credits cover generation + embeddings.
- Commitment: 6-month rolling commit with graded ramp (month 1 = 40%, month 2 = 70%, month 3+ = 100%).
- Committed spend triggers per-token discounts according to tiers in the attachment:
  - >= $50k/mo commit: 15% off list per-token price
  - >= $100k/mo commit: 25% off list per-token price + preferential queueing for burst capacity
  - >= $250k/mo commit: 35% off + dedicated capacity option (discounted Dedicated uplift)
- Credits do not replace discounts; credits are promotional balance consumed before billing.
- Requirement to secure credits: signed MAP + PO referencing deal id VER-2026-0615. PO can be standard net-30. If you need a refundable hold instead of PO for the pilot, we can evaluate on a case-by-case basis.

Next steps:
1) If agreeable, Ill send the MAP and a short SOW + pilot T&Cs for execs/legal to review.
2) We can run the POC under hosted API; if you want VPC or Dedicated for the pilot we can discuss additional setup time and pricing.

I attached the credit & tier sheet and a template MAP. Happy to jump on a quick call tomorrow to finalize.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0142

Attachments: redwood_commit_credit_sheet_v2.pdf (PDF, 28KB), veridian_mutual_action_plan.xlsx (Excel, 12KB)
